gloss: An unknown quantity or unknown value.

A ray of short-wavelength electromagnetic radiation usually produced by bombarding a metal target in a vacuum. Used to create images of the internal structure of objects; this is possible because X-rays pass through most objects and can expose photographic film.
A radiograph: an image made with X-rays.
An X-ray machine, a machine for performing radiography.
A tactical motif where a piece exerts influence or control over a square, piece, or line indirectly through another intervening piece.
To take a radiograph of; to obtain an image of using X-ray radiation, especially for the purpose of medical diagnostic evaluation.
Of a piece, to exert indirect influence, by either attacking, defending, or controlling an opponent's or friendly piece through an intervening piece along a rank, file, or diagonal.
The axis on a graph that is usually drawn left to right and usually shows the range of values of an independent variable.
A mammalian sex chromosome: in the XY sex-determination system, cells of females typically have a pair of X chromosomes, while cells of males typically have an X and a Y.
A vision into the X-ray portion of the light spectrum, enabling visibility through certain solid matter.
The ability or superpower to see through most or all solid objects as if they were transparent.
A hack allowing players to see enemies behind walls or other solid objects.
The distance between the baseline and midline in a typeface, typically equal to the height of the lower-case letter x.

A theory that posits a common syntactic structure for different lexical categories. Each phrase (XP) is the projection of a head (X) and may optionally include a specifier (sister of X-bar, daughter of XP), adjuncts (sister and daughter of X-bar) and complements (sister of X, daughter of X-bar).
